title: Variant
description: A purchasable variant of a product with specific option selections.

id.description: Global ID (GID) uniquely identifying this variant. Used as item.id in checkout.

sku.description: Business-assigned identifier for inventory and fulfillment.

type.description: Barcode standard. Well-known values: UPC, EAN, ISBN, GTIN, JAN.

barcodes.description: Industry-standard product identifiers for cross-reference and correlation.

description.description: Variant description in one or more formats.

categories.description: Variant categories with optional taxonomy identifiers.

price.description: Current selling price. REQUIRED when `pricing` is absent or `pricing.mode` is `public` [PROPOSED: conditional requiredness — see `pricing`]. MUST NOT be present when `pricing.mode` is `quote_required` or `contract_only` [PROPOSED]. Price is the amount per one whole `quantity_unit.unit` (for example, per lb or per hour); when `quantity_unit` is absent, it is per `each`. Line total is `price × quantity × 10^-scale`, computed and rounded once by the Business; `totals` remain authoritative.

pricing.description: [PROPOSED — requires a TC-approved Enhancement Proposal] Pricing state of this variant in this response. `mode` describes how price is (or is not) advertised to the caller of *this response* — it is a property of the response, not a fixed property of the variant: the same variant may be `buyer_specific` to an anonymous caller and carry a numeric price for a linked buyer. Well-known modes: `public` (default; a numeric price is advertised and `price` is REQUIRED), `buyer_specific` (price depends on the caller; a numeric `price` MAY be present when this response is addressed to a recognized buyer, and MUST be treated as specific to that caller), `quote_required` (no price is advertised; the buyer must request a quote — `price` MUST NOT be present), `contract_only` (no price is advertised; pricing exists only under contract — `price` MUST NOT be present). A Platform MUST NOT display, infer, or compute a numeric price for a variant that does not carry one in the response, and MUST NOT treat a missing price as zero (note: `amount: 0` on a present `price` still means free).

mode.description: Pricing mode for this variant in this response.

reason.description: Business-defined machine-readable reason for a non-public mode (for example `contract_or_volume_dependent`). Informational only; consumers MUST NOT infer semantics beyond `mode`.

next_step.description: Well-known values: `request_quote`. What the buyer can do next to obtain a price. Informational only; it defines no quote, RFQ, or identity-linking workflow.

quantity_unit.description: Sale basis this variant's `quantity` is denominated in. The default sale basis is `each`, whose machine identity is (`C62`, 0); `C62` is the UN/CEFACT Rec20 code for one/each. An absent catalog descriptor encodes that default. An `increment` advertises the ordering granularity in steps (for example, `scale` 2 with `increment` 25 sells in 0.25-unit multiples).

list_price.description: List price before discounts (for strikethrough display).

unit_price.description: Price per standard unit of measurement, for shelf-style comparison display. MAY be omitted when unit pricing does not apply.

options.description: Option values that define this variant (e.g., Color: Blue, Size: Large).

media.description: Variant media (images, videos, 3D models). First item is the featured media for listings.

tags.description: Variant tags for categorization and search.

metadata.description: Business-defined custom data extending the standard variant model.

seller.description: Optional seller context for this variant.

allOf.description: [PROPOSED] Neither `price` nor `unit_price` (a per-unit selling price) may be present when the variant advertises no price in this response.
[PROPOSED] Price is REQUIRED for publicly priced variants (the default when `pricing` is absent).
[PROPOSED] `unit_price` is derived from the selling price and requires `price` to be present.
